name: hunger chess where pawns forage
summary: At the start of each of your turns you collect 1 coin for every piece of yours on your second rank, where your pawns start. You start with 10.
Every move costs coins: the further from your back rank a piece lands, the more it pays. A pawn pays 1 coin a rank, a knight, bishop, rook or queen 2 a rank, the king nothing.
A move you cannot pay for cannot be made. Instead of moving you may pass, unless you are in check.
Taking a piece earns you its booty from the bank: 1 coin for a pawn, 2 for any other piece.
A pawn that promotes pays for its own arrival and the new piece's: 21 coins for a queen.
description: Chess with supply lines where the pawns are the farm. Every move is paid for out of a purse, and a piece costs more the further from home it lands; the coins come from your second rank, a coin a turn for each piece of yours standing on it. At the start that is the eight pawns, so every pawn pushed is a coin a turn given up for the rest of the game, while the pieces behind them cost no income to develop, once a pawn has stepped aside to open their line. The opening becomes a question of which pawns to spend: each move that frees a bishop or a rook is paid for twice, once from the purse and again in every turn's income after it, and a piece that steps back onto the second rank earns again.
